unresolved.finding: Command-line arguments are read into a fixed 100-character buffer without checking truncation status, so a long option can be silently shortened before parsing.

All return codes from initialization, parameter lookup, time stepping, and output are overwritten without validation, so failed initialization can leave t or tstop undefined and failed steps can still loop or emit output.

The double-precision fill value is formed by converting the single-precision HUGE value, so it is only about -3.4e38 rather than a true double-range sentinel and can collide with or fail ordering assumptions for valid double values.
The nonstandard REAL*8 declaration assumes an eight-byte representation instead of using the module's dpkind kind parameter.
The slopecorr parmapply call stores its selected-name string in par%sedfricfac_str, overwriting the string field for a different parameter instead of a slope-correction string field.
nglobalvar input is capped at 20, while the built-in default path installs 21 global variables, leaving the explicit-input capacity contract inconsistent with the default.

The Snell-law default calculation reads thetamin, thetamax, and dtheta whenever single_dir is zero, although this routine assigns those directional-grid fields only inside the earlier swave==1 branch.
Depth scaling modifies par%maxerror unconditionally, although maxerror is assigned here only for stationary waves or single_dir mode.

The block says it only allows Baldock/Janssen in stationary mode and Roelvink formulations otherwise, but non-stationary Baldock or Janssen selections merely produce warnings and are neither rejected nor changed.
The tide/epsi post-check tests epsi < -1 even though the configured default is exactly -1, so the documented automatic-computation notice is skipped for the default sentinel.
The wave-current warning is entered for WAVEMODEL_STATIONARY but states that interaction with non-stationary waves is experimental.

distribute_par broadcasts the raw bytes of a derived type containing pointer descriptors and then repairs only three named pointers, a representation-dependent contract that is unsafe if the type gains other descriptor-bearing fields or MPI ranks differ in layout.
readPointPosition searches indefinitely for the section keyword using reads without IOSTAT, so a missing/malformed section reaches EOF without a controlled read error or termination path.
The backward-compatibility warning emitted when the legacy nonh parameter is present says nonh was specified using wavemodel, reversing the actual parameter relationship.
readkey_dbl parses every value with fixed-width F10.0, so numeric text longer than ten columns can be truncated or rejected even though the backing value buffer is much longer.
Legacy-name translation indexes allowed(j) for every old name without enforcing nov<=nv, so a caller that registers more legacy aliases than canonical names reads beyond the allowed array.

readkey_dblvec handles only negative IOSTAT after list-directed conversion; a positive IOSTAT from an invalid token is ignored and partially undefined vector elements are subsequently range-checked and returned.
readkey_intvec likewise ignores positive conversion IOSTAT and proceeds to inspect and return a partially undefined integer vector.

The scalar and vector readers assign results only on xmaster and leave non-master results undefined when bcast is false, but the public interfaces do not constrain bcast=false calls to master-only execution.

readkey caches key/value pairs in fixed 1024-element arrays but increments ikey for every line containing '=' without a capacity check, allowing a sufficiently large parameter file to index past both arrays.

The preprocessing routine replaces only non-printable characters and does not remove comments, so any comment text containing '=' is cached as a parameter and later reported as unknown or can interfere with value parsing.
setallowednames tests only presence of each name and then dereferences its paired optional integer without verifying that the integer is present, making malformed public calls undefined.
read_v_9 assumes optional outputs form a contiguous prefix (for example, presence of a8 implies a1 through a7) and dereferences/broadcasts earlier optional arguments without PRESENT checks.
The generic read_v routines and count_lines open/read files without controlled OPEN or READ error reporting, unlike the parameter readers elsewhere in the module.

parameter pointer components have no default NULL initialization, and getkey associates only the pointer matching the current type, leaving the other pointer components with undefined or stale association state.

All returned scalar pointers alias one of three shared SAVE temporaries, so a later getkey call of the same type silently changes the value observed through every earlier result and makes the API non-reentrant.
Introspection key lookup is case-sensitive even though the parameter-file reader performs case-insensitive key matching, creating two different naming contracts for the same parameters.
The exported parameter type advertises units, description, and dimension metadata, but getkey initializes none of those fields for a successful scalar lookup.

Every rank/type pointer in arraytype lacks default NULL initialization, so consumers cannot safely query association state on a newly created descriptor before the construction code explicitly initializes all unused alternatives.
The dimensions component specifies array shape twice (DIMENSION(maxrank) and an entity array spec of (20)), which is a conflicting Fortran declaration and is likely rejected by a conforming compiler.
arrayf2c returns a C pointer to the local target array a, whose lifetime ends when the function returns, and the pointer does not reference any data from farray.
stringlength records null-character positions without exiting and then unconditionally assigns size(char_array), so it always returns the full buffer size regardless of termination.
Each allocatable index array specifies DIMENSION(:) both as an attribute and again on the entity name, a duplicate shape declaration that conforming compilers can reject.
The public module-wide stencil-bound integers have no initialization, so any caller that observes them before the separate setup routine assigns every bound receives undefined state.
index_allocate and index_allocated do not validate index or reject an unknown choice, unlike indextos, so invalid requests can silently no-op or report a scalar-like allocated result.
space_distribute_vector treats every selector other than lowercase 'x' as 'y', allowing typos or unsupported selectors to choose the wrong decomposition silently.
The btype '2' distribution path allocates vectorg on every rank but deallocates it only on xmaster, leaking the pointer allocation on each non-master invocation.
space_who_has returns the undocumented magic value -123 when no computational domain contains a coordinate and emits no diagnostic, leaving callers to infer failure.
All four loc cases in space_collect_vector_real8 execute the identical collection and there is no default case, so loc currently has no semantic effect while invalid values silently do nothing.
space_collect_mnem passes chartoindex's -1 failure result to space_collect_index, which indexes sg%collected(index) before the later indextos range check can reject it.
Real variables of unhandled rank (notably rank 1) and unknown real cases fall through without collection but are still marked sg%collected(index)=.true., suppressing future attempts.
The collection end marker logs event_coll_start again, and the already-collected early return skips an end marker entirely, producing unbalanced or mislabeled MPE traces.

gridprops labels xzg11/yzg11 as the global grid origin but assigns them from the local array element (1,1), which is not the global origin on non-top/non-left MPI subdomains unless callers prevent local invocation.
Grid-cell inverse areas are formed by unconditional division by computed polygon areas (or metric products) with no local degeneracy/zero-area guard.
posdwn is transformed as posdwn*abs(posdwn), so permitted fractional inputs change magnitude (for example 0.5 becomes 0.25) rather than merely being normalized or sign-adjusted.

When hotstart is enabled the bathymetry reads are skipped, but grid_bathy still negates, boundary-copies, snapshots, and differentiates the allocated zb array before hotstart_init_1 later supplies its values.
The Delft3D comment-skip loop does not inspect READ IOSTAT before testing line(1:1), so EOF or a read failure before a non-comment line has no controlled exit.
All three MPI sends/receives overwrite the same ier and none is checked, so transfer failures are silently ignored.

Directional bin counts are computed with NINT and are not constrained to at least one; equal/narrow angle bounds can yield ntheta or ntheta_s zero, followed by zero-sized wave arrays and division by s%ntheta.
The swave==0 branch computes theta0 from par%dir0 even though all_input assigns dir0 only for selected boundary-condition types, leaving this path dependent on external/default initialization.
Prescribed-bathymetry timestamps are not checked for ordering or coverage of time zero, and the interpolation status returned in dummy is ignored when constructing the initial bed.
wave_init allocates Dp, umwci, vmwci, and zswci but the subsequent initialization block never assigns them.
spectral_wave_init opens the boundary file and reads its header without IOSTAT handling, despite later records having explicit format-error checks.
flow_init allocates qmag, dUi, dVi, cfu, cfv, zs1, sigz, and the vertical-profile arrays but does not initialize them in its extensive initialization block.
The hotstartflow iteration divides by s%cf even though flow_init explicitly set s%cf to zero and has not computed a friction coefficient before entering this block.
The hotstartflow force balance unconditionally uses rhoa, Cd, windsu, and windnv although rhoa/Cd are read only when wind is enabled and no wind-disabled guard is present here.
The stationary-flow fixed-point loop has no iteration limit or non-finite residual check, so a divergent or NaN-producing initialization can run indefinitely or exit with invalid state.
For a completely wet domain under instantaneous tide, the only code intended to populate zs0fac is commented out, leaving both tide weights at the earlier all-zero initialization.
D15 is always allocated but assigned only when dilatancy is enabled, leaving the array undefined in the other configuration even though it remains part of distributed state.
Single-fraction sediment forces every layer thickness to at least 10 m, whereas multi-fraction sediment uses dzg1/dzg2/dzg3 directly, creating a large unexplained behavior change solely from ngd.
Sediment-fraction normalization handles a near-zero total but never rejects negative individual fractions, so a positive total containing negatives is normalized into still-negative bed fractions.
sed_init allocates iwl, Tsg, vmag, ccz, ca, and refA but omits them from the subsequent initialization assignments (iwl is notably adjacent to initialized istruct).
For a v-oriented discharge in a ny==0 model, the n1 clamp first raises the index to 1 and then lowers it to s%ny==0, storing a zero grid index in pdisch.

Drifter indices are formed by adding unconstrained fractional offsets to the nearest grid index and converting to integer without clamping, so out-of-domain drifter coordinates can produce indices outside the arrays.
All low-level hotstart readers capture OPEN/READ IOSTAT but never inspect it, allowing format or I/O failures to leave restart fields partially undefined after existence/length checks pass.
timestep_init initializes four counters and four specific output flags but omits ith and outputh, which are later used to index tph and determine output.
File-supplied schedule counts are obtained by NINT from a real value with no nonnegative/integer validation, permitting negative allocation extents or a silently rounded record count.

Schedule files are neither sorted nor checked for monotonicity, while current-event detection advances in file order but tnext uses MINVAL over all future values, so an unsorted file can schedule a time that the index-based detector will not emit.
Fixed schedule construction divides by tintg, tintp, tintm, or tinth even though the parameter reader allows each interval to be zero.

outputtimes_update relies on MINVAL over zero-sized arrays and all-false masks returning the huge-value identity; the subsequent special-case comparison checks only huge(tpg), making this behavior implicit and compiler-semantics-sensitive.

Initial CFL calculations apply MINVAL/MAXVAL to stencil slices without checking that ranges_init produced nonempty ranges, which can occur for very small local MPI subdomains and yield reduction identities or invalid square roots.
Bed-celerity and sediment-diffusion reductions of par%dt do not update dtold, ilim, jlim, or limtype, so a later timestep-collapse report can attribute the limiting condition to the wrong cell/type.
In the 1D viscosity criterion mdx is a squared spacing, but when par%dy>0 mdy is assigned the unsquared spacing before mdx*mdy/(mdx+mdy), unlike the squared-spacing formulation used in 2D.
The SAVE variable dtref in timestep has no initialization before its first call to compute_dt, whose only initialization path requires dtref to compare equal to exactly zero.
No explicit positive/finite guard is applied to computed or caller-supplied dt before CEILING, time advancement, and dtref/dt ratio checks, so zero, NaN, or infinity can propagate into control logic.

File existence is checked only on xmaster and the error flag is never broadcast, so non-master callers requesting the optional exist result always report true even when the master found the file missing.
The check_file_length overloads open files without OPEN IOSTAT handling, so permission/open failures are reported only indirectly through a subsequent read.

Length/validity checks parse scientific input into default-real temporary arrays even though the consuming model generally reads real*8, so values valid in double precision can fail or overflow during the preliminary check.
check_file_length verifies only that at least the requested number of numeric values can be read and never detects trailing records/values, despite its name suggesting an exact dimensional check.

The 3D error path passes the error text as writelog's format argument rather than supplying the empty format argument used by the 1D and 2D overloads, yielding an inconsistent/malformed diagnostic call.
LOCLIST sets nlocs to every remaining physical line, including blank/comment lines, and then requires each to parse as a location record, with no filtering or declared file-format guard.
get_file_length uses hard-coded unit 11 rather than create_new_fid, so it can close or conflict with another file already connected to that unit.

get_file_length stops counting at the first nonnumeric/failed list-directed record and counts numeric records rather than physical lines, making the generic name misleading and malformed later records indistinguishable from end-of-file.
create_new_fid_generic can return the same unit on consecutive calls if the first caller has not opened it yet, because it reserves no unit and retains only a shared probe value.

linear_interp_2d uses global masked extrema to choose brackets without requiring X and Y to be monotonic; a nonmonotonic coordinate array can select nonadjacent indices and interpolate across unrelated Z cells.
mkmap documents covered=0 as the default but never initializes covered, so targets not found inside any source cell retain undefined status.
mkmap ignores bilin5's error flag and stores hbuff and reference indices even when the bilinear solver exits without defining its output weights.
Both mapping builders explicitly convert double-precision bilinear weights to kind-4 real before assigning them back into real*8 arrays.

A target on shared/overlapping cell boundaries can be processed repeatedly, and a later invalid or boundary cell can overwrite covered after an earlier valid cell set weights and references, leaving status and mapping data inconsistent.
make_map declares covered INTENT(OUT) but never initializes it globally, assigning it only for targets that pass a cell polygon test.
make_map also ignores bilin5's error flag and commits potentially undefined hbuff weights and valid-looking indices.
The mapping/sort path has no n2>0 guard; with zero targets it still calls hunt/indexx, whose implementations access xx(n), xx(1), or indx(0).
mkmap_step updates source-cell indices using unconstrained FLOOR offsets and builds four linear indices without clamping i1/j1 to 1:m1-1 and 1:n1-1.
mkmap_step divides by local dsu and dnv without checking for zero or degenerate grid metrics.
grmap validates only the first reference as positive; subsequent references are not bounded above by n1, and nonpositive references are coerced to f1(1) rather than rejected.
grmap2 checks that references are positive but never checks iref<=n1 before indexing f1 and cellsz1i.
ipon converts coordinate offsets from real*8 to real*4 before edge/intersection tests, making polygon classification sensitive to large-coordinate cancellation and small cells.
bilin5 returns ier=1 through label 99999 without assigning INTENT(OUT) w, while its two callers in this module use the weight buffer regardless.
trapezoidal double-counts when both integration limits fall in the same source interval: it adds a first partial trapezoid plus a middle full-cell contribution instead of integrating only x1 to x2.
trapezoidal has no n>=2, ascending/equidistant, nonzero-dx, or x1<=x2 validation before endpoint access, division, and index construction.

trapezoidal_cyclic constructs internal breakpoints at absolute multiples of dx rather than x(1)+k*dx, so an equidistant source grid with a nonzero phase origin is integrated across missed piecewise-linear breakpoints.
interp_using_trapez_rule unconditionally accesses xtarg(2) and divides by its spacing, with no ntarg>=2 or nonzero-spacing guard.
interp_in_cyclic_function assumes n>=2 and a positive nonzero dx/xcycle; zero or negative icycle leads invalid allocation/indexing and can make the wrap loops nonterminating.
When n>icycle+1 the routine labels the case nonsense but performs no error return and proceeds with uninitialized xc/yc arrays.
The interpolation fraction uses mod(xp,dx)/dx instead of the offset from xc(1), and MOD can be negative, producing wrong or extrapolative weights for shifted grids and negative target coordinates.

fftn truncates an overlong dim list but never validates each dimension index or rejects duplicates, so zero/out-of-range entries index shape illegally and repeated entries are transformed/scaled multiple times.
fftn does not require positive shape entries or guard PRODUCT overflow before using the product for scaling, loop bounds, and transform strides.
fftradix returns immediately for npass<=1 without defining optional INTENT(OUT) stat, after which fftn tests that undefined status value.
When a present dim array has zero length, fftn performs no fftradix call and never defines the caller's optional INTENT(OUT) stat.
hilbert evaluates log(real(m)) and derives an FFT allocation size without checking m>0, so a zero-length input enters log(0) and invalid integer/exponent calculations.
hilbert accepts a complex input array but explicitly copies only real(xi) into the transform buffer, silently discarding any imaginary component.

flipa's flip==1 branch loops to M1 while indexing the second dimension and assigns whole columns, causing out-of-bounds access when M1>M2 and duplicating column-flip behavior instead of flipping rows.
xerf maps NaN inputs to +1 because both magnitude comparisons are false and the fallback branch is selected, masking the non-finite input.
random seeds with iabs(j) without handling the most-negative integer, whose absolute value is not representable and can leave an invalid negative seed.

POSIX usleep is declared as a void subroutine with a signed c_int argument even though the C function returns int and takes useconds_t, leaving the binding nonconforming and allowing negative or overflowing delays.

The fallback calls a nonstandard sleep routine after truncating microseconds to whole seconds, so unsupported compilers silently lose subsecond throttling and depend on an undeclared platform-specific interface.

In the non-MPI multi-record-jump path, both q1 and q2 are assigned from gq2, so the earlier discharge record gq1 read at lines 612-615 is discarded and temporal interpolation uses the later record at both endpoints.

Several Surfbeat and nonhydrostatic taper expressions divide by par%taper without the positive-taper guard used by the stationary branch, so an allowed zero taper would produce invalid boundary values.
The par%order==3 nonhydrostatic monochromatic branch contains only commented assignments, leaving s%zi and s%ui stale while accepting the option.
The TS_NONH MPI path does not broadcast isSet_V, yet every rank tests it to set s%vi and s%isSet_Vbc, so non-master ranks use an undefined logical.

TS_NONH discharge-to-velocity conversion guarded by isSet_Q exists only in the non-MPI preprocessor branch, so MPI runs distribute raw discharges as boundary velocities and also never broadcast isSet_Q.
All four hybrid-tide minimum updates call min with the corresponding maximum accumulator instead of the minimum accumulator, corrupting the observed ranges used to compute the hybrid coefficients.
Hybrid relative error divides by the maximum observed range without a positive floor, so constant water-level windows can yield division by zero.
Saved Coriolis coefficient fc is initialized only when par%t<=par%dt, so a first invocation after a hot start or externally managed time can use an undefined value.
Vertical point discharges are clamped into each local subdomain and applied with no ownership test, causing every MPI rank to inject every point source at a local edge cell.
An unrecognized scalar/vector mode is silently accepted and leaves saved lVarU at its prior value, so malformed or changed files can be parsed using stale layout state.
Saved header indices iZ/iU/iV/idU/idV/iQ/iW/iT are not reset when a new boundary file is initialized, so variables absent from the new header can retain indices from the previous file.
Although the time-column index iT is detected, data columns are always addressed as header_index-1, implicitly requiring time to be the first header without validating or documenting that constraint.
For a boundary file with only one time level, EOF handling sets t1 equal to t0 and then immediately performs interpolation divided by t1-t0.

When EOF is reached during or before a regular call, values and isSet_Q are assigned but isSet_U/isSet_V/isSet_Z/isSet_W/isSet_dU/isSet_dV are not, despite all being intent(out) and subsequently consumed by callers.
Tidal gradients divide by boundary distance differences (or s%dnz for 1-D) without validating nonzero spacing, so a degenerate or repeated boundary coordinate produces invalid gradients.

The local maximum bed elevation is computed only over imin:imax,jmin:jmax, but maxloc searches the entire row or column, so halo or non-boundary values can supply a distance unrelated to maxzbl in decomposed domains.
Spatial interpolation uses reciprocal endpoint or ridge-to-end distances without guarding coincident endpoints or a maximum located exactly at the relevant endpoint.
In case 4 on a lateral boundary, points beyond the separating maximum receive tide2 but are assigned tidegradient1 rather than tidegradient2.

fill_tide_grid updates each local interior from its local cross-shore maximum and local boundary endpoints with no MPI reduction or global-coordinate reconstruction, and the source itself states this only works for cross-shore-strip decompositions.
An empty or unreadable tide file yields s%tidelen=0 and is then indexed as s%tideinpt(0) in the duration check.
The tide timestamps are accepted without checking that they are strictly increasing, although subsequent linear interpolation depends on a usable ordered time axis.
An empty or unreadable non-stationary wind file yields s%windlen=0 and is then indexed as s%windinpt(0) in the duration check.
Non-stationary wind timestamps are not checked for strict monotonicity before later time interpolation.
The module exposes no public procedure, its only proposed generator is entirely commented out, and its sole active state variable initialized is unused.

Nearly all scalar components of the module-global saved state lack default initialization, so safe use depends on every consumer completing an external initialization sequence that the types themselves do not enforce.
The file named as the wave-boundary initialization unit is completely empty despite the datastore contract naming wave_boundary_init as one of its consumers.
Dummy argument nspr is used with present(nspr) but is never declared, which is invalid under implicit none.
MOD does not map negative input angles into [0,2π), contrary to the stated invariant, because a negative dividend produces a negative remainder.
waveBoundaryParameters%randomseed is declared as a scalar integer in the datastore but is passed to allocated/deallocate as if it were allocatable.

After first initialization, changed geometry, dimensions, file name, reference position, depth, or random seed are silently ignored while optional controls continue to change, leaving a mixed old/new configuration.
isRecomputed is intent(out) but is assigned only when a new series is generated, so calls before the next generation deadline return it undefined.

A time jump spanning multiple series durations generates only one new series rather than advancing until startComputeNewSeries exceeds t, leaving administration and interpolation potentially behind the requested time.
When BUILDXBEACH is not defined, the advertised cross-model path contains no interpolation implementation and returns eebc, qsbc, and qnbc without assignment.
lastwaveelevation is allocated under a comment saying it is initialized to zero, but no value is assigned before later reuse as spectral continuation state.
fid is assigned only inside BUILDXBEACH but the OPEN and subsequent I/O are outside that guard, so the non-XBeach build uses an undefined unit number.
err is tested by the LOCLIST counting loop before it has been assigned.
The single-spectrum branch sets local nspectra=1 but never assigns waveSpectrumAdministration%nspectra, leaving the stored count undefined.

The main generator references undeclared par, s, and bcfiles, assigns misspelled undeclared durantionlength, and contains an unmatched endif at line 240, so this routine cannot compile under implicit none.
The repeatwbc branch never initializes local wp, yet the routine obtains the returned duration from wp%rtbc after that branch.
Each spectrum location can overwrite the shared wp%rtbc and wp%dtbc, but no check requires all locations to use the same series duration and sampling interval.

Deallocating containers such as specin, specinterp, scaledspec, vargen, and combspec does not deallocate their pointer components, and tempSf and avgscale are also left allocated, causing repeated-generation memory growth.
The generator increments only the module shortcut bccount and never writes it back to waveSpectrumAdministration%bccount, so later calls continue to behave as the first boundary series.
The partition iteration explicitly permits scalefac1 to become zero and then divides by scalefac1 in its convergence metric, producing infinities or NaNs.
After zeroing all but the dominant partition in each overlapping spectral cell, the final assignment rebuilds every scaledspec from the full original partition, discarding the overlap mask.
A fully removed partition can make the peak-based ratio compute 0/0, and the resulting ratio-minus-one is then described as percent energy overlap even though it is a pointwise amplitude scaling.
SWAN relative-frequency input (RFREQ) is detected but the documented conversion to absolute frequency is a no-op marked STILL TO BE DONE.

Readers index the second direction element and pass frequency/direction axes onward without enforcing at least two bins and strict monotonic order, despite later integration and interpolation depending on those properties.
The code explicitly allows a non-monotonic input frequency axis but computes signed cell widths and passes that same axis to interpolation routines that require an ordered coordinate.
The zero-directional-interpolation fallback indexes specin%S with the standard-grid index i, which can run to 801 even when the input spectrum has fewer frequency rows.
Wave direction, peak frequency, and representative-period calculations divide by spectral sums without guarding an all-zero or threshold-empty spectrum.
set_repeatwbc references bcfiles without qualifying it through waveSpectrumAdministration or declaring a local alias.
The nonhydrostatic frequency cutoff uses g*k*tanh(kh)/(2π) instead of sqrt(g*k*tanh(kh))/(2π), giving dimensionally and numerically incorrect cutoff frequencies.
The directional PDF is normalized by its discrete sum but its trapezoidal CDF is not renormalized to end at one, so upper-tail random draws lie outside the constructed CDF range.
MOD can return a negative generated direction, contradicting the stated 0<=theta<2π invariant.
If no spectral bin survives the threshold and cutoff, frange returns coincident default indices, leading to dfgen=0 and subsequent division by dfgen.
wp%rtin is recorded as tslen*dtin while the generated time axis ends at (tslen-1)*dtin.
generate_wave_time_axis assigns ind_end_taper even though that name is neither declared locally nor present in the datastore.
Wave-train variance rescaling divides by hm0post without guarding a zero interpolated spectrum.
Spatial spectrum interpolation neither rejects coincident spectrum positions nor guards sfnow=0 before rescaling by sfimp/sfnow.
generate_swts is called with two arguments (wp,s) but is defined with only wp.
lntheta and ldtheta are never assigned before allocation and looping, wp%WDindex is used without allocation, and par_px is undeclared.
The wraparound-bin test uses binedges(i,...) where i is the wave-component index up to K rather than binedges(itheta,...), so it can read outside the directional-bin array and tests the wrong bin.
The lost-energy percentage divides by lostvar+keptvar without a zero-total-energy guard.
generate_ebcf repeatedly uses undeclared ntheta, s, lastwaveelevation, and ind_end_taper instead of the available datastore-qualified fields.
Inside the iy loop, a scalar elevation for point iy is assigned to the entire lastwaveelevation(:,itheta) vector, so each boundary point overwrites continuation state for all points.
Directional envelope scaling divides by stdeta without handling a zero total excitation.
Each loop iteration assigns one scalar time to the entire interior tbc slice, leaving all finite time entries equal to the last loop value.
The resampling branch queries (it-1)*dtbc for an output slot corresponding to (it-2)*dtbc, while the no-resampling branch assigns a tslen array into a tslenbc slice without ensuring equal extents.
generate_qbcf uses undeclared s, tslenbc, and non-BUILDXBEACH interpolation symbols, preventing a valid build as written.
Difference-wave group velocity and interaction coefficients divide by k3 and a resonance denominator without masks for zero or near-zero values.
Phase is computed with log of Fourier coefficients that can be exactly zero for zero-amplitude components, propagating undefined phases into later complex products.
Boundary unrolling multiplies K-shaped matrices by whole npb-length distx and disty arrays rather than distx(j) and disty(j), producing nonconformable shapes or unintended element mapping.
qxbct is allocated twice while qybct is never allocated, so the second allocation fails and later qybct assignments target an unallocated array.
Long-wave resampling repeats the one-step time offset and unchecked tslen-to-tslenbc shape assignment used by the energy path.
Saved work arrays and scheme selections are initialized only on the first call, so reuse with changed grid dimensions, directional bins, or scheme parameters keeps stale shapes and settings.
The condition admits 2kh values up to 3000 but evaluates sinh(min(2kh,10)), while values just above 3000 are set to 3000, creating an inconsistent discontinuous approximation to sinh(2kh).
Mean wave direction is computed as an arithmetic energy-weighted angle, which gives incorrect results for energy distributed across the 0/2π wrap.
Wet-cell wave energy is divided by s%sigm without enforcing a positive intrinsic frequency.
Directional dissipation distributes only breaking and bed-friction losses even though the source comment explicitly identifies missing vegetation dissipation Dveg.
The wave-flow smoothing factors are not capped at one, so large hydrodynamic timesteps can make the old-state coefficient negative.
Second-order directional advection is enabled for any ntheta>1 but indexes itheta+2 at the lower boundary, which is out of bounds when ntheta=2.
The dispersion loop can only exit with iter<=itermax, so the post-loop test always reports success even when the iteration reaches its limit without satisfying the error tolerance.
breakerdelay operates only on local cross-shore coordinates and history with no inter-rank exchange, and its own source explicitly states that it is not MPI compliant.
Multiple saved work arrays are allocated only on first use, so changed grid dimensions or enabling WCI after an earlier non-WCI call can leave wrong shapes or unallocated WCI arrays.
An unsupported useAverageDepthSwitch value is silently accepted and leaves hhlocal and possibly velocity work arrays holding stale values.
The WCI depth weight uses 1-h/hwcimax without a nonnegative clamp, so depths above hwcimax reverse rather than suppress the current contribution.
Radiation-stress force stencils leave several subdomain-edge Fx/Fy values unset and perform no neighbor communication, a gap explicitly identified by the inline comments.
Wet-cell Stokes and roller drift divide by phase speed and hstokes without enforcing positive denominators.
All saved work arrays are sized only on the first call, so reuse after a grid or direction-count change retains incompatible shapes.
Multi-direction mean wave angles are computed by arithmetic averaging rather than circular vector averaging, failing for spectra spanning the 0/2π boundary.
The sinh(2kh) approximation has the same discontinuous <=3000 test with an internal cap at 10 and a fixed 3000 value above the test.
Wave energy is divided by per-direction intrinsic frequency s%sigt with no positive-frequency guard.
thetaadvec is subtracted every call but is reset only when refraction is enabled, so disabling refraction after prior enabled calls preserves an old refraction tendency.
Orbital velocity is evaluated over the full grid before any wet mask, dividing by sinh(kh) at potentially zero-depth cells.
Roller dissipation divides by the magnitude of directional phase velocity without guarding a zero-speed wet cell.

Wave-crest boundary interpolation constructs nx+3 coordinate and value entries by adding two infinite endpoints but passes nx+1 as the interpolation length, silently excluding part of the constructed support.

After scaling directional roller energy using equivalent height RH, total roller energy s%R is capped directly against gammax*hhw (an energy-versus-length comparison) instead of being recomputed from the scaled rr or converted height.
Saved arrays and the lateral-advection scheme are fixed on first call, so later grid, direction-count, cyclic, or scheme changes retain stale state.
The sinh(2kh) approximation repeats the discontinuous <=3000 test with a cap at 10 and a fixed 3000 value above the threshold.
Arithmetic angle averaging mishandles wraparound spectra, while the Snell branch passes an unclamped ratio to asin and can leave its real domain.
The cross-shore CFL denominator uses maxval(cgx) rather than maxval(abs(cgx)), so a field of large negative propagation velocities yields an excessively large timestep.
The full row slab is divided by s%sigt without a wet mask or positive-frequency floor.
The breaker-height correction evaluates H/(gammax*hh) over all cells without excluding zero-depth dry cells, allowing 0/0 and NaN energy.
Orbital velocity is computed without a wet/depth guard before its use in bed-friction dissipation.
Both the roller update and reported roller dissipation divide by directional phase-speed magnitude without a positive floor.
Several Fy boundary entries are deliberately not assigned, so the saved model state can retain values from an earlier stationary solve rather than a defined boundary condition.
The routine computes current roller drift s%ustr but always forms total drift from s%usd, without calling breakerdelay here or selecting ustr when breaker delay is disabled.

Common saved arrays are dimensioned using the first callType's direction count and never resized, although the routine is designed to be called in both stationary and directions modes with potentially different ntheta values.
An unsupported callType leaves ntheta_local, hhwlocal, ee_local, and dtheta_local undefined rather than rejecting the call.
The sinh(2kh) approximation repeats the discontinuous <=3000 test with a cap at 10 and a fixed 3000 value above the threshold.
Both modes use arithmetic mean angles that fail across 0/2π, and stationary Snell refraction passes an unclamped value to asin.
Wet-cell energy is divided by s%sigm without checking for a positive intrinsic frequency.
The directions-mode dissipation uses s%Dveg even though the source notes it has not been updated for the stationary-direction wave height.
Roller theta-advection is applied unconditionally in stationary mode even when par%refraction disables the corresponding wave-energy theta-advection.
Roller dissipation divides by directional phase-speed magnitude without a positive floor.
After scaling rr by a height-based gamma factor, s%R is assigned RH*gammafac, a length, rather than the corresponding roller energy or the sum of scaled rr.
Relative H error divides by zero wave height, while the EE metrics build a wetmask but never apply it, allowing dry or halo cells to control convergence.
Non-convergence logging caps both H error and direction error at 0.99, hiding the true magnitude of larger failures.
Final orbital velocity is evaluated over the full grid without a wet/depth guard.
The saved gamma work array is never resized if the grid dimensions change.
The new hstokes path computes H/hh across the full grid without a positive depth floor, so dry zero-depth cells can produce invalid gamma and zero hstokes.
Wave updates depend on the timestep landing within 0.001*dt of an exact wavint multiple, so non-commensurate dt and wavint values can skip all later scheduled updates.
The update schedule evaluates mod(t,wavint) without validating a positive nonzero wavint.
Saved administration is initialized only when t equals dt within 1e-6, so hot starts or externally managed first calls can use undefined reuse, counter, bcendtime, rt, and dt.
testc is read only by the master but is tested on every rank to set saved reuse, with the corresponding broadcasts explicitly commented out.
The CLOSE intended for the last timestep is placed after RETURN and can never execute.
For a minimal 2-D grid with ny=1, the offshore-depth average uses empty slices and divides by a zero sum.
The parametric directional grid includes both -π and π and normalizes them with a rectangular sum, double-counting the identical periodic endpoint.
SWAN RFREQ input is recognized but its conversion to absolute frequency is a no-op.
SWAN keyword searches perform reads without IOSTAT or EOF handling and can loop indefinitely on a truncated or malformed file.
SWAN and VarDens inputs are used without requiring at least two directions or strictly increasing frequency and direction axes, despite direct second-element indexing, quadrature, and interpolation.
An empty threshold range makes M zero and a single-bin range makes K=1 and df=0, causing divisions by M, K-1, and df.
Hm0 correction divides by hm0now and directional-width construction divides by S0 without a zero-energy contract; the small S0 floor does not protect hm0now.
Generated frequency indices are written into CompFn without verifying that they lie below the Nyquist slot or within the Nr-length FFT array.
Nbin is never initialized, and a direction shifted once by 2π can still fall outside a computational sector narrower than 2π, leaving its bin entry undefined before maxval and nspr handling.
If no generated time sample is at or below rt, temp is all zero and the taper divides by maxval(temp)=0.
Directional envelope amplitude divides by stdeta without handling a zero total elevation signal.
The expressions size(array-1) return the full sample count rather than size(array)-1 as the surrounding standard-deviation comments imply.
Symmetric parametric energy redistribution tests WBCTYPE_PARAMS even though this generator is entered for WBCTYPE_PARAMETRIC, so the intended parametric branch may never run.
The synthesized record starts at t=dt, but record 1 is written as the first boundary sample and the consumer treats direct-access record 1 as time zero.
Bound-wave group velocity and interaction coefficients divide by k3 and a resonance denominator without zero or near-resonance masks.
Bound-wave phase takes the logarithm of Fourier coefficients without excluding exact zero coefficients.
Difference-wave direction uses atan(KKy/KKx) with a signed epsilon instead of atan2, losing the correct quadrant whenever KKx is negative.
Flux rotation derives its angle from atan(qy/max(qx,eps)), which replaces every negative qx with a positive epsilon and therefore gives incorrect quadrants and components.
Representative-period formulas divide by spectral moments without guarding zero energy or, for Tm-1,0, zero frequency.
bc_disper evaluates 0/0 for zero angular frequency and divides by h without enforcing a positive boundary depth.
The last-step early return occurs after incrementing bccount and before assigning the INTENT(OUT) curline, so the caller receives an undefined line while the global sequence advances.
The catch-up loop can call a spectrum reader repeatedly on the same spectrum object, but the readers allocate its pointer components again without first deallocating or nullifying them.

Each location may overwrite wp%rtbc and advance its own end time, while the global end time is advanced only from location 1 and the saved/admin duration is taken from the last location, with no equality check.
Cyclic direction adjustment derives the boundary span from point max(ny-2,1) rather than the far offshore-boundary endpoint, making the intended ghost-cell/physical-span contract unclear.

Cleanup deallocates containers with pointer components without freeing their pointed-to spectra and variance arrays, and it omits vits, duits, dvits, and the nonhydrostatic WDindex, allowing repeated boundary generation to leak substantial storage.
JONSWAP-table Tp is read directly with no positivity validation and is immediately used as 1/Tp and to construct dfj.
The TMA correction divides by tanh(k*h0) and normalizes by sqrt(sum(y)) without guarding zero boundary depth or a collapsed spectrum.
SWAN RFREQ input is explicitly marked as still needing conversion to absolute frequency, yet both RFREQ and AFREQ branches currently leave the frequency vector unchanged.
File-provided frequency and direction counts are not validated, while later code unconditionally accesses angle element 2 and adjacent-angle differences.
The readers do not sort or reject nonmonotone axes—even noting that SWAN frequencies are often nonmonotone—while endpoint range tests and linear_interp calls assume an ordered frequency axis.
Pre-interpolation variance uses signed local df and dang values on axes described as potentially nonmonotone, so m0 can be negative before sqrt(m0).
Zero-energy spectra are permitted by the readers but derived direction, peak frequency, and representative-period calculations divide by zero-energy sums without a fallback.
MOD is used to normalize the mean direction, but Fortran MOD preserves a negative dividend and can leave dirm below zero.
Boundary filenames encode exactly five decimal digits with CHAR(48+i), so bccount above 99999 produces non-digit characters and possible filename collisions or invalid names.
The nonhydrostatic frequency cutoff assigns g*k*tanh(kh)/(2*pi) without the square root required to convert dispersion-relation omega-squared to frequency.
The trapezoidal cumulative directional distribution is not normalized after integration, so its final value is generally below one although draws span the full [0,1) interval.
Cyclic adjustment computes L_wave/sin(alfa_wave) with no branch for a wave parallel to the grid span, relying on floating-point infinity behavior.
If thresholding and fmax remove every component, MAXLOC returns index 1 for both ends, producing dfgen=0 and a later division by dfgen.
rtin is set to tslen*dtin although the generated axis ends at (tslen-1)*dtin, leaving duration conventions off by one sample.
Per-location variance is rescaled by (hm0/hm0post)^2 without checking hm0post, which can be zero for a location with no selected-frequency energy.
Spatial spectral interpolation rescales by sfimp/sfnow without guarding sfnow=0.
wp%PRindex is allocated inside the offshore-point loop, so the second point attempts to allocate an already-associated pointer.
Findex is derived from dfgen even though the actual FFT spacing is 1/(tslen*dtin), and ceiling/even-length adjustments do not ensure those spacings are equal.
Components above the upper directional edge receive WDindex=lntheta+1 and are excluded from all physical theta bins, but the diagnostic counts only WDindex=0 as lost.
Directional envelope amplitudes divide by stdeta without guarding a zero total elevation series.
Energy scaling and directional percentage reporting divide by unguarded mean and total energy, including the bclwonly zero-envelope path.
The two-layer velocity formula guards nhlay>0 but not nhlay=1, where z is zero and the u2 division by -z is singular.
The bound-long-wave interaction coefficient divides by a dispersion-mismatch term that can approach or equal zero, with no resonance tolerance or cap.
Bound-wave phase is obtained with LOG of Fourier coefficients without excluding zero-amplitude components, for which complex log is singular.
When dtchanged is true qinterp has only three fields although the file record length and reader contract are four fields, unlike the non-interpolated write of q(:,:,:).
The nonhydrostatic administration-file open and write collect iostat but never test it, so list-file failure is silently ignored.
The superharmonic cutoff tests k3(m,1), but for m>K+1 valid entries start above column 1 and k3(m,1) remains its initialized zero, disabling the intended cutoff.
Superharmonic phases access Findex(1)+ii and +jj instead of the component indices Findex(ii) and Findex(jj), shifting every lookup and reaching beyond the last generated component.
Six-field storage and qx/qy layer arrays are allocated only when nonhq3d=1 and nhlay>0, but later branches test only nonhq3d=1 and can access those arrays when they were never allocated.
Layer flux ratios divide by sinh(KKx*h0) and sinh(KKy*h0) without limits for axis-aligned interactions where KKx or KKy is zero.
The upper-layer ratios subtract sinh(KKx) or sinh(KKy) rather than an interface-depth product, leaving a dimensioned wavenumber as a hyperbolic-function argument and omitting z.
Second-order layer flux is converted using q1/z and q2/(h0+z), even though z is negative and the lower and upper layer thicknesses are h0+z and -z respectively.
The second-order routine computes qy1 and qy2 time series but never adds them to vits or dvits when assembling the nonhydrostatic boundary signal.
When bwdefaults.inp is absent only the scalar defaults are assigned, so an absent shoreline source can leave bw%sigS uninitialized even though errS and sig2obs use it unconditionally.
Source 4 is documented and processed as observed wavenumber data but assim_rd stores it in bw%cobs rather than bw%kobs, after which bw%kobs is read without any visible initialization.
The backtracking loop has no guard for zero dsc or zero/invalid averaged L1, so disfac can be zero and backdis can fail to advance indefinitely.
The dispersion calculation divides by s%hh over every grid point before the wet-cell mask is tested, so zero-depth dry cells can produce division by zero or NaNs.
The celerity expression adds dimensional Hrms to dimensionless rk*s%hh inside tanh, making the implemented dispersion relation physically unclear.
ntimesnew is accepted without a 1..999 bound, while the time-advance loop always reads itimnew+1 and relies on a sentinel that cannot be placed safely for 1000 or more records.
The entire uncertainty-file read path is commented out, leaving statuserr at zero even when fnameerr is supplied and causing configured observation-error maps to be silently ignored.
Hb and its derivative divide by or evaluate singular hyperbolic ratios at s%k or kh without a positive lower bound, so zero-wavenumber cells can generate invalid values.
Nassim is computed as tstop/dt although the adjacent change note says it was changed to tstop/wavint, leaving the intended assimilation-count scaling contract contradictory.

After erosion sets isveggie false, subsequent calls fall through the unconditional elsewhere branch and can rebuild bedfriccoef from the original vegetated nman0, so the apparently permanent vegetation-removal state does not prevent roughness regrowth.
Manning friction is clamped to both mincf and maxcf at initialization but only to maxcf during updates, allowing the advertised lower bound to be lost after the first update.
The grain-size White-Colebrook update hard-caps cfu at the literal 0.1 while cfv uses par%maxcf, creating an unexplained directional difference and bypassing the configured u-direction cap.

For the last v row the interpolated infilb boundary is assigned directly from s%infil(:,s%ny) rather than copied from the adjacent interpolated v-point as done for the u boundary, producing an asymmetric boundary treatment.
Dynamic Manning roughness divides by dstem and droot with no local nonzero check, leaving its parameter contract implicit.
White-Colebrook formulas divide by kru/krv and take log10 without locally enforcing positive roughness heights, so validity depends entirely on upstream input constraints.
Turbulence stresses use the signs of s%ue and s%ve while neighboring bed-stress code uses s%ueu and s%vev, leaving the intended staggered velocity/sign convention unclear.

In MPI mode a drifter outside every subdomain is stored near HUGE(real), but the next active call converts that sentinel with NINT before recognizing it as out of range, which can overflow the default integer.
MPI_MIN is applied independently to idrift and jdrift, so if different overlapping ranks produce the minima the reduced coordinate pair need not come from any single rank's drifter update.
The update checks only array-domain bounds and never the wet masks, leaving behavior over dry cells dependent on whatever values uu and vv carry there.
Strict time inequalities skip updates exactly at both configured drifter start and end times, an endpoint convention that is not documented locally.
The 1-D vertical-momentum path does not clear wrk1 globally and cycles inactive mask cells before zeroing them, so a flux left from an earlier call can enter an active neighbor's divergence.
The negative-v continuity correction lacks the leading minus used by the analogous negative-u branch, making the qy correction's sign inconsistent with the qx implementation.

Cross-advection of v uses s%dsu(...,1) throughout a two-dimensional loop and the first negative-flow gradient uses dsu(ie,1) for the i-to-ie interval, which is inconsistent with local curvilinear spacing.

The continuity correction repeatedly fixes the unused metric coordinate at 1 (dsu(i,1), dnv(1,j), dsz(i,1), dnz(1,j)), despite the module claiming curvilinear support and looping over the full 2-D grid.
Second-order velocity corrections divide by hum, hvm, or hh without a local positive-depth guard at the update point; the broader stencil mindepth check does not protect every update path.

Module work arrays are allocated once with the first grid shape and have no reinitialization or shape check, so repeated library initialization with a different grid would retain incompatible storage.
Neighbor masks are multiplied and used as a real flux factor rather than reduced logically, so the code silently assumes mskZ values are strictly binary rather than merely zero/nonzero.
The left global boundary calls flow_lat_bc with par%right while the right global boundary passes par%left, apparently swapping the configured lateral boundary types.

s%ue at i=nx+1 and, in 2-D, s%ve at j=ny+1 are not assigned, yet the vertical-profile loop consumes both arrays over 1:nx+1 and 1:ny+1, so wet edge cells can use initialization-era or stale velocities.

Several staggered interpolants (vu/vsu/usu and uv/vsv/usv) update only interior slices and explicitly leave some process-edge rows or columns unresolved; multiplying by a wet mask does not refresh previously wet, still-wet omitted entries.
The Smagorinsky cross-stress dudy term for v uses wetv(i-1,j) as its fourth mask while the other three factors and the differentiated field are u-point quantities, suggesting one wetv should be wetu.
hu and hv are clamped nonnegative before flow_secondorder_huhv, but the second-order correction can subtract from them and there is no subsequent positivity clamp before forming qx and qy.
When viscosity is disabled the code zeros nuh and viscu but not viscv, so a reused state that changes viscosity mode can retain the previous y-momentum viscous acceleration.

Old-state arrays are allocated only if second-order or nonhydrostatic mode is active on the first call; because later allocation is gated by vsu, enabling either mode on a reused instance would access unallocated uu_old, vv_old, and zs_old.
All saved work arrays and bed-roughness initialization are keyed to a one-time allocation test with no grid-shape or parameter-change check, making reinitialization semantics implicit.
qmag combines qx and qy elementwise even though they are stored at different staggered locations, so the stated output magnitude lacks an explicit interpolation convention.
The cell-centered vertical-profile call derives ks directly from u-point cfu(i,j) without documenting interpolation or guarding the positive-friction prerequisite.
The fast 2-D parabolic solver loops on i but indexes A and rhs with k, which remains zero from line 817, causing index-zero writes.
The fast 2-D exponential solver loops on k but never sets i, then uses the initialized value i=0 in grid and coefficient subscripts, causing invalid indexing.
The fast 2-D solver assigns x(:,1), sized nx+1, into gwhead(2:nx,j), sized nx-1, in both head-model branches.
The full 2-D solver builds and solves coefficients only for the parabolic model, but afterward accepts the exponential model and computes a head from gwcurv that this branch never solved.
The 1-D matrix builder tests k==-1 and k==-n inside a positive 1..n loop, so both intended endpoint branches are unreachable and endpoint off-diagonal treatment falls through to the interior formula.
Exponential-head formulas divide by groundwater thickness at cells where gwheight can legitimately be zero at the aquifer bottom, with no limiting form or dry-cell guard.

infilcon is first allocated as independent storage and later pointer-associated with s%infil through the hydrostatic function, orphaning the original allocation and making later mode behavior depend on aliasing.
The v-interface infiltration availability limit uses s%hh*s%dsz for the surface-water volume while the groundwater side and all v-direction area scaling use dnz, creating an x/y metric mismatch.
All turbulent conductivity fixed-point loops have no iteration cap or non-finite escape even though maxiter is declared elsewhere in the module, so a nonconvergent cell can stall the timestep.
Local infiltration divides by dt/por and later by dis and infil without guarding zero conductivity, zero timestep, zero porosity, or a zero computed infiltration distance.
dwetlayer is used as a divisor in both the smoothing ratio and hydrostatic infiltration cap without a local positive-width check.
The 1-D system allocates n unknowns and maps all n entries back to the grid but calls solver_tridiag with n-1, leaving the intended solver dimension ambiguous.

Interface-height output leaves the last u or v row assigned only on a physical bottom/right rank and performs no halo exchange here, so internal process-edge values rely on unstated caller or solver behavior.
Updated Kx, Ky, and Kz are all smoothed only along the i direction, including Ky, with no explanation for the directional treatment.
Several select-case blocks have no default assignment, so an unsupported groundwater scheme or head model can leave logicals or numeric outputs undefined unless validation is guaranteed upstream.
At a right MPI boundary uev_sed(:,1:ny+1) is assigned from uev_sed(:,1:ny), a nonconformable array assignment that appears intended to copy only the final column.

cub/cvb already include the active-layer pbbed fraction before bed-load transport is formed, but Sub/Svb are multiplied by another upwind pbbed factor afterward, apparently squaring fraction availability.
Inside the i,j loop the representative-size update assigns scalar sums to the entire D50top and D90top arrays rather than to (i,j), leaving every cell equal to the last loop cell.
Avalanche deposition edg1 multiplies edg2 by sedcal a second time, so erosion and deposition masses differ whenever a sediment calibration factor is not one.
update_fractions loops until an exact floating-point zero and has no escape when dzbt becomes zero because a limiting layer thickness is zero, so dzb_loc may never decrease.
intra_sedtr allocates SAVE allocatables unconditionally on every call, so its normal use from repeated transus timesteps will attempt to allocate already allocated arrays.
Nielsen2006 allocates fe only when streaming is enabled but assigns fe=0 unconditionally, accessing an unallocated array when streaming is off.
Both smoothed bed-load implementations set the top boundary from qsedu(i,:) after the i loop has finished, when i is nx+1, instead of using the top boundary or adjacent cell.
intra_sedtr computes ceqbg by dividing Subg by hh*uu before zeroing subcritical transport, so zero velocities generate NaN or infinity that the later Subg mask does not remove from ceqbg.
The negative-slope branch for y-direction Nielsen correction tests dzbdx<0 instead of dzbdy<0, skipping or misapplying the alongshore slope correction.
Bulk McCall-Van Rijn concentration is formed as qsedu/(hu*uu) over the whole array without a wet or nonzero-velocity mask.
In 2-D turbulence advection disturb is assigned only when betad>0 but is used unconditionally in the kturb update, leaving it undefined for betad<=0.
At zero v velocity, kturbv is averaged from its own just-zeroed values rather than from neighboring s%kturb values, forcing the centered face turbulence to zero.
During groundwater-coupled erosion tempexchange is a water-depth amount but is added directly to the infiltration rate without division by dt, unlike the accretion branch.
dzbdt is updated only for single-fraction transport before avalanching; multi-fraction changes and all later avalanche changes update zb/dzbnow but are omitted from dzbdt.
update_fractions sizes saved work arrays from nd(1,1) and never checks the current cell's nd(i,j), so spatially varying layer counts can exceed or mismatch the workspace.
The bed-slope exclusion applies only to the Svb half of an OR expression, so any nontrivial Sub enters the Soulsby adjustment even where bermslopeindexbed is true.
Wave-asymmetry velocity components average adjacent ua values but use the first cell's sine/cosine for both terms, rather than rotating each adjacent vector with its own angle.
Several sediment-velocity interpolants leave nx+1 or ny+1 entries untouched except on selected physical boundaries, yet full-array magnitudes and transports consume those entries.
The Surfbeat berm-slope condition evaluates H/hu across the array without protecting zero hu before the logical selection.
Transport and slope directions use atan(y/x) with manual quadrant handling and still divide by zero for vertical vectors, rather than a two-argument angle function.
Alongshore avalanche scaling omits the max((Sig/grid)^2,1) lower bound used by the cross-shore branch, producing unexplained direction-dependent rates.
The code explicitly notes that copying interior bed state into Neumann boundary cells introduces a bed-volume mass error, and no compensating flux or accounting is present.
Fall-velocity reduction raises 1-ccg to a noninteger power without bounding concentration below one, so out-of-range concentration creates NaNs.
Bore turbulence divides by Tbore and the runup jet uses indexed hh in a square-root denominator without local positive guards or index validation.
The lagged velocity filter uses dt/(cats*Trep) without clamping it to [0,1], so large timesteps produce negative old-state weights and overshoot.
Slope/dilatancy factors take square roots of algebraic radicands and later sqrt(srfTotal) without enforcing nonnegativity, so steep or roundoff-affected states can become NaN.
The Soulsby-Van Rijn velocity cap divides by s%cf without the positive lower bound used by the neighboring Van Thiel branch.
Van Rijn 1993 activates bed load using nonnegative speed ue but computes and divides by signed used=vmg+ua, allowing negative or singular equilibrium concentration.
The vertical integration grid divides by kmax-1, so kmax=1 is unsupported without an explicit parameter guard.
Nielsen friction and streaming divide by Arms while its initial or still-water value can be zero; the streaming transition can also divide by abs(umeanupd)=0.
Fredsoe-Deigaard branches clamp dimensionless bed slope with reposerad (an angle) rather than reposedzdx (its tangent), unlike the corresponding Nielsen implementation.
Streaming regime tests compare uvarupd, a squared-velocity statistic, directly with abs(umeanupd), a velocity.
intra_sedtr defines ratio_s=(rhos-rho)/rho but then uses ratio_s-1 in dstar, unlike the same standard calculation elsewhere in the file.
Turbulent bed stress uses sign(1,taubxsed), which is positive at exactly zero base stress and therefore imposes a positive x direction in still water.
Suspended-load calculations use taubx_turb even when lwt is disabled, while this routine assigns that array only inside the lwt branch.
The analytical concentration profile divides by hh-za and the final depth average divides by hh without handling the hh=za or zero-depth limits.
Relative-weight correction divides infiltration by Kzinf with no lower bound, so impermeable cells make facrw invalid.
The turbulence update divides by hh over active loop ranges without an explicit wet/depth guard, relying on an upstream depth floor.
The Ursell number divides by (k*hh)^3 before applying its lower clamp, so zero k or depth yields non-finite intermediate values.
Bore-slope calculations divide by sigm and, in the mean branch, by an unbounded max(c,sqrt(Hg)), allowing zero-wave states to create invalid values.
Multiple saved workspaces are allocated once from the first grid and option set with no shape or option-change checks, making library reuse with changed configuration unsafe.
vmag takes sqrt(max(vmag2,umin)), comparing squared velocity with a velocity-valued threshold.
nonh_init allocates module work arrays unconditionally, so a second initialization or a grid-size change without an intervening teardown can fail or retain an incompatible module lifecycle.
The legacy solver stores only dsu(:,1) and dnv(1,:) and later uses those fixed cross-sections throughout the domain, leaving the full-2D curvilinear-grid contract unclear.
In the one-layer excluded-point bottom-slope correction, the west bottom slope is assigned from dzs_e rather than dzb_e, mixing the surface and bottom geometries.

The two-dimensional excluded-point surface-slope branch assigns dzs_n from dzb_s when both V points are wet and clears dzs_e/dzs_w, rather than dzs_s/dzs_n, in its fallback, so the y slopes can be wrong or stale.
The corresponding bottom-slope branch assigns dzb_w from dzs_e and its final fallback clears the x slopes instead of dzb_s/dzb_n, leaving erroneous y-direction bottom slopes.
Reduced two-layer formulas divide by wcoef, 1-wcoef, and nhlay-nhlay**2 without a local bound excluding 0 or 1, so endpoint layer coefficients make the predictor or stress terms singular.
The MPI left-boundary clause repeats Wm(1,:)=Wm(2,:) instead of setting Wm(:,1), so the left y boundary is not populated as the surrounding top/bottom/left/right pattern indicates.
The 3D U predictor uses wcoef(i,j) for both neighboring pressure coefficients, unlike the analogous 2DV expression which uses wcoef(i+1,j) on the eastern contribution.
The 3D V predictor forms its surface-slope coefficient with zs(i,j)-zs(i,j+1), the opposite orientation to both its bottom term and the analogous U-direction expression.
The lower-layer V-velocity friction calculation uses s%cfu rather than the V-point friction field s%cfv.
The V-point corrector averages wcoef(i,j) with wcoef(i+1,j), using an x neighbor where the V staggering calls for the j+1 neighbor.

nonh_init_wcoef accepts an unconstrained explicit dispc and computes the optimized value through a denominator that is neither checked nor bounded, despite downstream singularities at endpoint or invalid coefficients.
disper iterates solely on an error tolerance with no iteration cap or invalid-input guard, leaving termination dependent on unstated positive finite inputs.
For ny<=2 the V-point free surface is filled from one fixed zs column (column 2 when present) for every j, rather than from the matching column, and the special-case intent is unclear.

Non-master ranks return before rainfallrate and the input arrays are allocated, while rainfall_update can subsequently interpolate into those components; this file only broadcasts the scalar constantRainfall flag.
The sole initialization of constantRainfall on non-master ranks is conditional on rainfall_update first being called with t<=dt, leaving it undefined if the first update occurs later.
The time-series path passes nrainfallrate and the file timestamps directly to LINEAR_INTERP without locally requiring at least a usable number of records or ordered, distinct times.
The rainfall file open has no iostat check, and the read-error branches rely on report_file_read_error to terminate before partially filled arrays are used.
All saved allocatable workspaces are sized only on their first call and never checked against the current grid dimensions, so reuse after a grid-size change is unsafe.
The non-Daly Roelvink formulas divide by hhw over complete rows or full arrays before restricting the result to an active region, with no wet mask or positive-depth floor in this routine.
The Daly branch deliberately retains Qb inside the hysteresis band but also leaves dry-cell Qb unchanged, after which dissipation is recomputed from that potentially stale value.
ROELVINK2 and ROELVINK_DALY multiply dissipation by H/hh without a local wet mask or positive hh guard.
The Baldock calculation floors k only in the Hb denominator while kh and the spatial gamma use the raw k, leaving negative or otherwise invalid wave-number inputs inconsistently treated.
The Janssen-Battjes implementation divides by raw k when forming Hb and by raw hh when forming D, unlike the neighboring Baldock implementation's k floor.

The breaking argument raises an unconstrained H-to-depth ratio to the real-valued parameter n, so a negative ratio with non-integer n would produce an invalid result unless positivity is guaranteed externally.
Ship-grid dx and dy permit zero, yet they define all coordinates and the cell area passed to grmap2, so a configured zero spacing creates a collapsed mapping grid.
ship_init allocates the ship pointer graph and global ship arrays without an allocated/associated guard or teardown, making repeated initialization unsafe.
A track with fewer than two records is accepted by count_lines, but automatic heading calculation unconditionally accesses records 1 and 2 and the final record minus one.
When compute_motion is enabled, zhull is not initialized, yet shipwave reads it to compute pressure before the later placeholder motion update; with compute_force disabled it is never updated at all.
shipphi, shipchi, and shippsi are allocated but not initialized, while the unimplemented motion branch immediately uses shipchi and shipphi to position the hull.
Heading is represented as a wrapped angle and then interpolated linearly without unwrap handling, so tracks crossing the angle branch cut can rotate through the long arc.
The saved firstship flag is cleared permanently after one call and has no reset path, so a subsequent simulation in the same process will skip its required initial surface adjustment.
Hull rotation and force moments subtract ship-local xCG/yCG values from globally positioned x/y coordinates, causing lever arms and rotated elevations to depend on the domain origin.
The local-grid origin uses integer division nx/2 and ny/2, producing an asymmetric set of coordinates for odd grid dimensions.
Ship-list, geometry, and track opens and reads have no visible status checks here, so malformed or short input depends entirely on helper-side termination behavior.
solver_free deallocates the work arrays but never resets initialized, so a later solve skips solver_init and uses deallocated storage.

Solver parameters and workspace shape are captured only on the first initialization; repeated initialization can double-allocate, while later solves with changed dimensions or parameters silently reuse the old state.
itmin starts at zero and is updated with min(it,itmin), so the reported minimum iteration count can never become positive.
An unrecognized solver value still marks the module initialized, and solver_solvemat then takes no branch and returns the input x unchanged without an error.

The Thomas solver divides by each pivot with no protection in its normal caller; the optional fix is not passed, and even when enabled it only catches values below machine tiny rather than numerically small pivots.
The SIP factorization divides by 1+p1, 1+p2, and p3 without singularity checks; adding a fixed small value to p3 does not prevent exact or near cancellation.
When bnorm is zero, epslin remains exactly zero and the strict rnorm<epslin test cannot succeed even for an exactly zero residual, forcing all maxit iterations.

Under MPI the factorization and forward sweep use the reduced local imin/imax/jmin/jmax bounds, but backward substitution always sweeps 2:nx and 2:ny, including cells whose factors and residuals were not produced in that iteration.
The documented SIP stability range for alpha and positive accuracy/iteration settings is not enforced locally before those values control factorization and termination.
Positive vegetation-map values are used directly as veg(ind) subscripts without checking ind<=nveg, so an out-of-range species code causes invalid access.
The gridform select has no default branch, leaving vegtype uninitialized if an unsupported grid form reaches this routine.

swvegatt cumulatively adds each ah value as a layer thickness, while momeqveg treats each ah value as an absolute section height corrected by bed change, so the same vegetation profile has incompatible vertical interpretations.
Short-wave vegetation dissipation is evaluated without a wet mask and divides by sigm, while its hyperbolic terms use raw hh, allowing dry or zero-frequency cells to generate invalid values.
totT is initialized only when t equals dt exactly; otherwise the nonlinear branch tests an undefined saved value and may read the still-unallocated unl and etaw arrays.
Saved vegetation work arrays are allocated only on their first call and never checked against later grid dimensions.
The above-wave-crest branch zeros the mean and nonlinear forces but not FvgCau/FvgCav, so enabling vegcanflo can reuse a canopy force from the previous section or cell.
Nonlinear and in-canopy force terms divide by raw hh for every vegetated cell without a wet or positive-depth guard.
swvegnonlin divides whole-domain arrays by hh and hh**3 before any wet-cell restriction, including in its Ursell-number and lookup-coordinate calculations.
trapz integrates only 49 intervals for the 50-point periodic profile while the caller supplies Trep/50 spacing, omitting the closing interval from the last sample back to the first.
bulkdragcoeff divides by sigm, sinh(k*hh), bveg, and alfav**0.76 without local guards, despite being callable with bed-adjusted plant height and shallow wave state.
porcanflow overwrites vegetation forces only on interior staggered-loop bounds, leaving the remaining boundary entries dependent on initialization or prior calls.
The species-list read records iostat but never checks it before the names are used as filenames.
delta is assigned only when omega>0 but is used unconditionally immediately afterward, so a nonpositive frequency reads undefined state.
The phase speed omega/k is formed before either operand is validated, so zero k can fail before the later cw>0 branch provides any neutralization.
dhdx and dhdy are read to form the first bottom-stress estimate before either variable has been assigned.
The main profile formulas divide by h, omega, and cw outside their protective branches, so zero depth or frequency remains singular even when tauwav and Qw were zeroed.

The viscosity-profile construction takes multiple logarithms and divides by sigmas, sigs1, phis, and their differences without checking the required ordering or nonzero conditions; clipping delta to 0.5 can also undo its lower bound relative to sigma0.
The routine accepts arbitrary n but divides by n-1 and accesses sigz(2), requiring n>=2 without enforcing it.
Gravity is hard-coded as 9.81 inside a model that otherwise supplies physical parameters externally, so profiles can be inconsistent with a configured model gravity.

Negative wave energy or breaking dissipation reaches square and cube roots without a local nonnegative-domain guard.

Every scheme value other than SCHEME_UPWIND_1 silently receives an upwind distance of two, leaving unsupported or newly added scheme values indistinguishable.
